evidence: The view uniform buffer has no ViewToClipNoAA, which arrived after 4.18, and every field after ViewToClip therefore sits 0x40 earlier than a later engine puts it. That shift is what made the stock layout stop predicting the buffer partway through, and correcting for it made the whole layout check out.
The velocity encoding matches 4.18's Common.ush exactly: written pixels average 0.4999928 against the 32767/65535 the source states, agreeing to seven decimal places.
D3D12RHI markers and the full D3D12 interface set are present in .rdata, consistent with 4.18 having it compiled in.
engine.notes: Vendor branch rather than stock: the view uniform buffer stops matching the stock layout in its later half even after the ViewToClipNoAA shift is accounted for, and the stock 2640 byte view buffer size does not occur at all. Treat stock offsets as hypotheses past the fields verified in ac7-frame-capture.md.

executable_protection.evidence: Shannon entropy 7.997 across all 38.9 MB of .text on disk, the PE entry point in a trailing .bind section belonging to the Steam DRM wrapper, and no reference anywhere in the file to the d3d11.dll or dxgi.dll import slots. Only .rdata is plaintext.
executable_protection.consequence: Static analysis answers nothing about code. Every hook site and offset here came from the module as it exists in memory after the wrapper decrypts it.

velocity.encoding_detail: In * (0.499 * 0.5) + 32767/65535, taken from Common.ush rather than fitted to captured data: in a frame where little moves the samples cannot determine the scale, and a fitted value came out wrong by four times while looking entirely reasonable.
velocity.camera_motion_evidence: Measured from replayed pixels rather than assumed: 83.6% of a camera-panning frame is exactly zero, and in flight the sky stays zero while sweeping across the screen.
velocity.notes: Written every frame by ten draws while the shipped settings present neither temporal antialiasing nor, in these captures, motion blur. The buffer exists because the engine's infrastructure wanted it, not because the game uses it, which is exactly the case worth looking for in other games.

jitter.detail: PreVisibilityFrameSetup computes a sub-pixel offset only behind View.AntiAliasingMethod == AAM_TemporalAA, and the menu offers no setting that selects it. Stepping over one conditional jump, six bytes at RVA 0x112b1f3, runs it whatever the menu says.
jitter.verified: Every perspective view carries an offset afterwards where all fifty earlier captures were exactly zero. Converted through the engine's own construction: -0.147, +0.065 and -0.430 pixels, all inside the half pixel a sample pattern produces.
jitter.field_layout: current x, current y, previous x, previous y, in clip space

temporal_pass.detail: A pass binding colour, a history target, velocity, depth and a 1x1 exposure target appears in every capture. Earlier notes named it FRCPassPostProcessTemporalAA from that input signature, which was inference and not proof, and this game does not run that anti-aliasing mode at all.
temporal_pass.notes: Accumulates without sub-pixel jitter, so it stabilises specular and cloud rendering and gains no resolution. Replacing its consumer rather than restoring it is the point: 4.18's own temporal antialiasing is what the developers had and chose not to ship.

render_scale.detail: In 4.18 that one variable is the whole mechanism: it shrinks the scene buffers through ComputeDesiredSize, makes ViewRect differ from UnscaledViewRect so the upscale pass appears, and the jitter formula divides by ViewRect so the offset rescales by itself.
render_scale.resets_detail: Loading a mission re-applies the game's own graphics settings and puts the value back to 100. A backend fed the presented size afterwards is doing antialiasing while looking like a success, so the scale has to re-apply itself.

insertion_point.recognised_at: the pass that binds colour, depth and velocity together at render resolution
insertion_point.detail: The pass that names the resources is the lighting. A capture replay shows twenty seven further draws adding the sky, the clouds and the translucency to that same colour target afterwards, and taking the colour where the set is recognised produced a reconstruction of a world with a black sky. None of the three inputs is written again once the colour is finished, so the evaluate happens at Present.
insertion_point.notes: The interface is composited before the game's own upscale, so at reduced scale it is upscaled with the scene. Reinserting before that composite is what would let the grade and the HUD survive; drawing over the finished frame, which is what happens today, loses both.

result.detail: In flight with the render scale held at 1024x576 against a 2048x1152 output: 7917 frames evaluated, none refused, and the reconstructed frame is the whole scene with no smearing under movement.
not_yet: Reinserted into the game's pipeline. The result is drawn over the finished frame, so it is ungraded and carries no interface.
Built with MSVC. Everything here is cross-compiled with mingw-w64 and tested under Wine.
